title: Occurrences After Bigram
statement:
`text` is a sentence of words separated by single spaces. Look for every spot where the word `first` is directly followed by the word `second` and then by one more word. Return the list of those following words, in the order they appear in `text`.

Spots may overlap, and the same word can play several roles (it can be the follower of one spot and the `first` of another). A `first second` pair at the very end of `text` has no follower and contributes nothing. Return an empty list when there is no such spot.
constraints: text contains only lowercase English letters and spaces
Words in text are separated by exactly one space
text has no leading or trailing spaces
first and second contain only lowercase English letters
signature: String[] findOcurrences(String text, String first, String second)

examples.name: Example 1
input: alice is a good girl she is a good student

examples.name: Example 2
input: we will we will rock you

tests.name: Test 8
input: a good a good a good

tests.name: Test 9
input: jump over jump over the fox

tests.name: Test 10
input: the cat sat on the cat mat the cat

notes:
## Intuition

Searching the raw string for `"first second "` is fiddly: the match must start and end on word boundaries, and occurrences can overlap. Splitting `text` into words removes all of that. Then the question becomes: for which positions `i` do the two words just before it equal `first` and `second`? One pass over the word list answers it.

## Approach

1. Split `text` on single spaces into `words`.
2. For every index `i` from `2` to the last word, look at the two words before it.
3. If `words[i - 2]` is `first` and `words[i - 1]` is `second`, add `words[i]` to `result`.
4. Return `result`; it is already in text order.

## Example 1, step by step

`words` is `[alice, is, a, good, girl, she, is, a, good, student]`, `first = "a"`, `second = "good"`. At `i = 4` the two previous words are `a` and `good`, so `girl` is added. No other `i` matches until `i = 9`, whose previous words are again `a` and `good`, adding `student`. The result is `["girl", "student"]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L), where L is the length of `text`: splitting and one scan over the words.
- Space: O(L) for the list of words.

## Pitfalls

- Compare whole words, not substrings: `"abc"` must not match inside `"abcd"`.
- Start `i` at `2` so both `i - 2` and `i - 1` exist; a final `first second` pair has no follower.
- Do not skip ahead after a match; occurrences overlap, as in `"we will we will rock"`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `words` | the words of `text` in order |
| `result` | the words found right after `first second` |
| `i` | index of the candidate third word |

narration.2: Break the sentence into its words; spaces are single, so split(' ') is exact.
narration.3: Collect the words that follow each first-second pair.
narration.4: Treat each word from index 2 on as a possible third word.
narration.5: Check that the two words just before it are first and second, in that order.
narration.6: They are, so this word follows the bigram; record it.
narration.9: Return the followers in the order they appeared.
